title: Unified Training Framework Combines All AI Model Training Stages Into Single Algorithm
summary:
A newly released machine learning method seeks to eliminate the traditional boundaries between the different phases of building artificial intelligence foundation models. The system, called Unified Training, merges pretraining, midtraining, supervised fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning (RL) into a single maximum-likelihood objective, which allows developers to train static and RL-generated data within the same framework.

Building on the MaxRL method, the approach aims to simplify the infrastructure required for model development and lower compute costs. The researchers state that this unified process reduces the likelihood of models forgetting previous information and enhances their ability to solve complex reasoning tasks compared to traditional staged pipelines.

selectedTweets.text:
New work on Training Foundation Models with a Single Algorithm:

Paper: https://t.co/bH6eDSgSbd
Code, Models: https://t.co/TDiMe3qLUM

This work introduces Unified Training, a framework that unifies pretraining, midtraining, supervised fine-tuning and RL under a single maximum-likelihood objective. Building on MaxRL, it enables static data and RL-generated data to be trained together within the same system. 

Empirically, Unified Training improves accuracy and compute efficiency, generalizes better to harder reasoning problems, and reduces forgetting. 

Interestingly, reusing data across training stages can improve performance even when conventional staged training fails. It also produces models that adapt more effectively to new tasks, leading to stronger continual learning.

See an excellent thread by @yus167.
